blocks.text: Charles Darwin was an English scientist. In 1831 he travelled as a naturalist on a scientific expedition aboard His Majesty's Ship Beagle, a five-year voyage around the world.

blocks.alt: A schematic dashed route joining the main stops of HMS Beagle in order: England (Plymouth, December 1831), Cape Verde Islands, Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, Tierra del Fuego, Chile, the Galapagos Islands in red (September 1835), Tahiti, New Zealand, Australia, South Africa and back to England (October 1836). It is not drawn to geographic scale.
blocks.caption: The main stops of HMS Beagle (original schematic after Figure 24.1).
blocks.long_description: In 1831 Charles Darwin sailed as naturalist on HMS Beagle, a five-year scientific voyage around the world. The ship crossed the Atlantic to South America, worked along its east and west coasts, crossed to the Galapagos Islands in 1835, then sailed across the Pacific and Indian Oceans by Tahiti, New Zealand, Australia and southern Africa, returning to England in 1836. The observations Darwin made on the voyage, especially on the Galapagos Islands, shaped his theory of evolution.
